parameters.content:
## ppwr-exception-review

Where an item the engine could not decide gets decided by a person.

**Why it exists.** `indeterminate` is the engine saying it could not tell: a field the document contradicts, a value read too poorly to trust. Before this workflow, an item that reached `in_review` had nowhere to go, because nothing else here can move it.

**Only what the engine could not decide is offered.** A check that came back clean is not on the form and a reviewer cannot overturn it. What moves is the one thing the engine said it could not judge.

**Every decision needs a reason**, and the field is mandatory. A decision no one explained is worth nothing to the auditor this project exists to serve.

**Rule feedback is recorded, never applied.** A reviewer spotting that the check itself is wrong is the most useful signal in here, and it belongs in the next ruleset version, not in a rule quietly edited under a campaign that already launched.

**The new verdict comes back from the engine's own summariser.** If a second copy of that logic lived here, the day the two disagreed a supplier would be told one thing and the record would say another.

**Access.** The form is open to anyone with the link and the submission id. Put it behind your own access control before pointing real reviewers at it.

Code nodes are built from `src/` by `npm run bundle`.

### Load

The submission, its findings, and who the supplier is. No writes on this lane.

### Decide and record

Reviews and findings, then the submission, then the state change, then the supplier.

parameters.formDescription:
A submission the screener could not decide on its own. You are deciding only the points it could not judge; everything else it checked stands.

This screens declarations for completeness and internal consistency. It is not a conformity assessment, it is not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a technical file or a notified body.

nodes.name: Exception review (page 1: identify)
nodes.notes: The submission id comes from the reviewer notification 03 already sends. Nothing about the submission is shown before it is asked for.

nodes.name: Defaults
nodes.notes: Ship-time defaults, overlaid by the meta table. The same settings 03 runs on, read the same way.

nodes.name: Load settings
nodes.notes:
Soft. A deployment with no meta rows runs on the defaults instead of failing.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes:
Defaults with the meta table laid over them, so every node downstream can read $('Configuration') and not care where a setting came from.

Built from src/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

value.key: ={{ { submission_id: String($('Exception review (page 1: identify)').first().json.submission_id || $('Exception review (page 1: identify)').first().json['Submission id'] || '').trim() } }}

nodes.name: Load submission
nodes.notes:
Verified against a live instance: a Form Trigger keys its output by the field's label, while a Form node keys by its name. Both are read here instead of guessing which, because the difference is invisible until a submission id arrives empty and the store refuses a get with no key.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Load campaign item
nodes.notes:
Read from the submission instead of from the form, so a reviewer cannot decide one item's findings against another item's state.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Load packaging item
nodes.notes: Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Load vendor
nodes.notes:
Soft. A missing vendor row must not stop a decision being recorded; it only means nobody can be told about it.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Load findings
nodes.notes: Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Open findings for review
nodes.notes:
The questions are generated from the findings, so a new check needs no new form field. A submission with nothing indeterminate fails here instead of presenting an empty form.

Built from src/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

nodes.name: Page 2: decide
nodes.notes:
The questions are generated from the findings, so a new check needs no new form field. The fields parameter is a fixedCollection, which is why they are handed over as JSON: an expression on the collection itself does not validate.

Accept means the supplier's answer stands and the check passes. Reject means it does not and the check fails. Override means the check does not apply to this item.

nodes.name: Apply decisions
nodes.notes:
A missing decision or a missing reason fails here, not downstream.

Built from src/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

nodes.name: Review rows
nodes.notes: Built from src/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

nodes.name: Write reviews
nodes.notes:
The durable record of who decided what, and why.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Finding updates
nodes.notes: Built from src/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

nodes.name: Resolve findings
nodes.notes:
Only the status changes. The check, the severity and the evidence stay as the engine wrote them, so the record still shows what was originally made of it.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Assess verdict
nodes.notes:
The engine's own summariser, so there is exactly one definition of what counts as conform.

Built from src/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

nodes.name: Update submission
nodes.notes: Mode is 'each'.

value.transition: ={{ { campaign_item_id: $('Assess verdict').first().json.campaign_item_id, submission_id: $('Assess verdict').first().json.submission_id, from_state: 'in_review', to_state: $('Assess verdict').first().json.verdict, event_type: 'review_' + $('Assess verdict').first().json.verdict, actor: 'reviewer:' + $('Apply decisions').first().json.reviewer, payload: $('Assess verdict').first().json.event_payload } }}

nodes.name: Record review transition
nodes.notes:
The actor is the reviewer, by name. A state change nobody can be traced to is not much of an audit trail.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Route verdict
nodes.notes: Two ways out, and in_review is not one of them: every indeterminate finding has just been decided.

nodes.name: Build cover request
nodes.notes: Built from src/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

nodes.name: Draft covering paragraph
nodes.notes: The same fenced job as in 03: the model writes around a finished list and the notice builder fails the execution if it mentions a check that is not in it.

nodes.name: Build gap notice
nodes.notes: Built from src/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

nodes.name: Build confirmation
nodes.notes: Built from src/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

parameters.completionMessage: ={{ 'The submission is now ' + $('Assess verdict').first().json.verdict + '. Your reasons are on the record against each finding.' }}
